title: Free County of Burgundy
capsule: The Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté, Latin: Comitatus Burgundiae) had been an imperial fief since the late tenth century; the Wikidata attestation from 1333 corresponds to the period when it passed under the Capetian house of Evreux through inheritance before coming to the Valois dukes. In 1384 it was united with the Duchy of Burgundy under Philip the Bold after the death of Count Louis II of Male, giving the Valois Burgundian state its eastern anchor on the Saône. The county passed to the Habsburgs in 1477 following Charles the Bold's death and was only definitively incorporated into France by Louis XIV under the Treaty of Nijmegen in 1678.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's core territorial extent in the Saône-Doubs corridor is well documented; the Wikidata period 1333–1385 captures a specific inheritance episode within a longer polity history and its boundaries for those decades are secure.
